top_review_amazon: Happy hydrating! Finally got a Stanley , and what perfect timing! Needed a new water bottle and got this beauty at an awesome price, and what a fabulous color! --- Matcha Cream!!  Is a Stanley cup worth it? ( I got the 40 ounce Quencher Flowstate )  Short answer, YUP. Well crafted, aesthetically pleasing, comfortable handle with thumb grip, temperature retention ( both hot and cold ) for impressively long hours, BPA-free, dishwasher friendly, 3 position lid. The lid is not 100% leak proof, but for me, this is not a deal breaker. Any spillage that you might get really depends on what you are doing with the bottle, and depends on positioning and how full your bottle is. Of course, you can buy straw covers (and other accessories) for your cup. The straw covers work without a problem, but not sure what can be done about the lid leaks. STILL, despite potential lid leaks, and despite being late to the craze, is this Stanley cup worth the hype and 5 stars? YES and YES.

top_review_amazon: I have been using this very frequently for over 10 months.  I did some research reading reviews and even read the one reviewer who compared the cost of the label refills.  I am so glad I chose the Dymo LabelMaker 160!What I love about this machine:1 - QUALITY - Never ever had an issue printing, it has been a reliable machine2 - Love the QWERTY keyboard.  An ABC keyboard would have driven me nuts.3 - It prints super clearly, even the off-brand refills that I bought.4 - Battery life has been forever.  In fact, I have not put new batteries in it yet (and I've printed the small roll it came with and almost a whole regular-sized refill).  I'm using regular batteries.5 - Lots of font sizes - from 8 to 24 with steps of 2 in between6 - Two lines of text - you can print one or two lines of text, wish I could do three though7 - Features - It has everything I need:  a few borders, many special symbols, text styles (not different fonts, just styles - italic, bold), can print vertical, etc.8 - Cutter works smoothly every time9 - Does not waste much label when printing10 - Nice size - It's not huge like some label makers.  It's also not tiny making it difficult to type what you need.  I had originally thought I wanted it even smaller but now, I'm thinking it's like the Goldilocks size, just right.Wish list:1 - Wish I could print 3 lines and not just 2.  There's enough room on the label in the smallest size but it doesn't do it.2 - Wish it had 2-3 fonts (not a ton, but more than one would be nice)3 - I wish the special symbols that I use most frequently would be in the first "row" of special symbols.  Like I think it's crazy that I have to tab down 8 times to get to the "&" symbol.  In fact, the 3-5 most frequently used symbols should be added to the keyboard.  Other than that, I don't mind that special symbols are accessed through a special button.  It's fairly easy and doesn't clutter the keyboard, keeping the machine a hand-held size.

This award-winning fresh goat cheese is distinguished by its fresh milk taste, mild flavor and smooth texture. description_amazon: Our favorite superfood comes from flax, one of the oldest fiber crops in the world - known to have been cultivated in ancient Egypt and China. Also called 'linseeds,' flaxseeds are a rich source of micronutrients, dietary fiber, manganese, vitamin B1, and the essential fatty acid alpha-linoleic acid, also known as ALA or omega-3. They are so powerful that King Charlemagne of the 8th century believed so strongly in the health benefits of flaxseed that he demanded his loyal subjects eat the seeds and passed laws to make sure of it. The Latin name for flax is Linum usitatissimum, which means "the most useful," and we couldn't agree more. Omega 3's are considered essential because they are necessary for human health and your body can't make them on its own. You need to get your Omega 3's through the foods you eat and flax is the perfect way to add them to your diet. And, flax seeds are one of the best plant-based sources of omega 3's available. Plus, a recent study from Penn State University suggests that plant-based omega 3 sources such as flax are likely just as effective as the well-publicized marine sources in preventing cardiovascular disease.

top_review_amazon: This review is for the strawberry variety of RX Bar. As I began to cook my own food from scratch more often, I found that I can no longer tolerate synthetic or poor quality foods. These RX Bars, when I can afford them, are a godsend for quick high protein meals on the go. Just pair it with a ready-to-drink protein shake and you're ready for the road. The quality of the ingredients range anywhere from good to excellent and the flavor is great. I would not recommend them for anyone with braces or dentures or anything because they are VERY chewy, have large pieces of almond or even whole almonds in them, and are rather sticky due to the dates and egg whites that act as sweeteners, binders, and protein sources. I appreciate the simple list of natural and wholesome ingredients, and I needn't worry about food sensitivities and adverse reactions to preservatives and fillers, plus they are a great source of fiber. Obviously they are not an option for anyone with tree nut allergies, but they are gluten-free, grain-free, and vegan. Probably not the best option for someone on a ketogenic diet, but they should work for paleolithic and whole foods diets, and I suppose even a justification for inclusion in a raw food diet could be made.

The large capacity and locking lid made this an easy choice for our needs. It’s a very nice model and highly recommended.

top_review_amazon: ****I am a product tester for Bates Choice and receive many items from the company, including these foam paintbrushes. I love these!  I really like how these work with stain - they hold quite a bit of stain in the foam and it's easy to control the flow of staining depending on how hard or soft you press down.  In general I prefer bristled brushes for painting, but these are great for jamming paint into small corners and holes in wood. She was in rough shape, as a trunk malfunction had resulted in damage to the hinges, and it could no longer close properly. On a normal car, this may not be such cause for alarm, but a convertible? The trunk opens backwards, yawning up to the sky to catch any and all debris, dry or wet! This unfortunate incident happened on a Thursday night, and the insurance company simply could not twiddle their thumbs about it until at least Monday.

I suppose you see where this is going, dearest Glad, for I live in Florida, where sudden storms (or, sometimes, long forecast storms) are the norm. Of course, such a storm was to hit on Monday, and I could not acquire a proper car cover in time, for a litany of reasons I will not dwell on.

Our story now takes us to Sunday night. I finished my bottle of Pinot Grigio (Yellow Tail, if you must ask! Such an underrated vintner) and observed in fascination as my ForceFlex bag sagged under the weight of the 1.5 liter bottle, but did not break! I had a sudden epiphany, not unlike the first bricklayer thinking to add a second layer. The bags! Of course! Armed with my ForceFlex bags, a pair of scissors, and some pink duct tape, I marched outside into the growing gloom, where storm clouds gathered overhead.

I employed all my wit as I carefully cut the bags and laid them out around the space where the trunk was open. A masterpiece! Not only had I protected the car from the storm, I had also singlehandedly reduced the property value of my area for a day. After I applied the last few pieces of pink tape, I adjourned inside. I rushed to bed like a child on Christmas Eve, excited to see if Santa truly does bring miracles, or just leaves soggy cookies on the mantle.

The next morning.

I steeled myself in my home once I woke up about noon. After 3 or 4 cups of coffee and an episode of Once Upon A Time, I remembered! The car! I rushed outside to see if my mad scheme had worked.

After rushing back inside to put some clothes on, I again returned to the car in my finest bathrobe, and behold!

A miracle.

The bags had performed wonderfully. They had deflected the rain off the edges of the car, as I'd predicted. In the middle, where the open trunk and back of the convertible top reached vainly to each other -a space of about 1 foot- something truly incredible happened.

The ForceFlex bag had filled with rain water and sunk into the trunk, molding to the shape of its surroundings. I estimated at least 2 gallons sitting comfortably in the trunk, trapped by the bag. I gingerly grabbed all the edges and lifted the bag slowly up and out of the trunk, and dumped the contents on the asphalt. And inside the trunk? Dry as a bone! Or as my bottle of wine. :(

So, from the bottom of my heart, thank you Glad ForceFlex bags. Whether I'm stuffing them with broken glass, or rainwater, or a suit for a wedding next week, I know you will never let me down!"}}

description_amazon: From grill to frying pan, Beyond Sausage® Hot Italian has a new, meatier taste and is the delicious hot sausage you're craving. It's also an excellent source of protein (16g per serving), has 0mg cholesterol, no added hormones or antibiotics and has 40% less saturated fat than a leading brand of pork sausage. Made from simple plant-based ingredients - like peas and brown rice - our Beyond Sausage has no GMOs, soy or gluten. Each pack contains 4 plant-based links that can be thrown in a bun, put on kebabs, sliced onto pizza or crumbled into sauce. Enjoy every bite. At Beyond Meat we believe there is a better way to feed our future and that the positive choices we all make, no matter how small, can have a great impact on our personal health and the health of our planet. By shifting from animal to plant-based meat, we can positively impact four growing global issues: human health, climate change, constraints on natural resources, and animal welfare. How Our Products Are Made: We source the building blocks of meat directly from plants. Using heating, cooling and pressure, we create the fibrous texture of meat from plant-based proteins. Then, we mix in fats, minerals, and carbohydrates to replicate the appearance, juiciness, and flavor of meat. The result? Uncompromisingly delicious plant-based burgers, sausage, and more, no sacrifice required.
top_review_amazon: I'm not a vegan or vegetarian, just someone who could no longer eat meat of any kind after watching a video back in 2016 on how living beings, no more or less important and sentient than humans, were being treated while alive, horrified me and to this day still breaks my heart - switched to Almond Milk that day as well (still eating fish and eggs & I struggle with both, but I simply can't do tofu/soy unless it's already prepared and doesn't look or taste like it so I need to eat something) Since then, I've been literally lost with not knowing what or how to cook all of my favorite foods, living on microwave food which is so bad for you. And to make matters worse, I recently needed to go Gluten-Free for medical purposes.I've already tried the Italian style meatballs, and they were good, I bought them again, but now after making the sausages I have a better idea on how to make them better and as good as these sausages (maybe hehe). BUT THESE SAUSAGES!!! OMG, you literally cannot tell they aren't meat in taste/flavor or texture! I haven't enjoyed sausage and peppers since early in 2016, likely 2015 or earlier. I'm eating it as I type this, because I was so shocked at how there's no way to tell they aren't meat sausages (aside from not having that body part gross "lining" they stuff the meat into thank God. These are FABULOUS! I'm enjoying my first "like I grew up on" meal for the first time in 7 years.For me, the best way to cook them, or how I did, which I didn't do with the meatballs, is put a little virgin olive oil in a small sauté pan, waited for it to warm up (I had the sausages frozen up until the day I was making them, they defrosted on the counter in less than 30 minutes, fabulous... ANYWAY, once the oil was nicely heated, I placed them into the pan and I literally cooked them until a second before they were too burnt to eat (on the outside). They weren't burnt, but close to burnt (outside). Then I cut them up into smaller pieces and placed them in a larger sauté pan that already had somewhat heated up crushed tomatoes (canned/organic and were fire roasted, so talk about flavor?)... needed NO additional seasoning whatsoever other than a little oregano that I threw in for a bit of sweetness, plus oregano is very healthy for many reasons, with also already somewhat heated 3 colors of peppers and a yellow onion in it. I let it all simmer for 3+ hours on very low heat, but it would/could have been eaten within 30 minutes, I'm just big on slow simmering for flavor and texture. Then I put it all in the fridge to eat the next day (leftovers always taste better to me and I'm finding with the plant-based meat it 100% tastes better the next day, but not before testing out the sausage, and it was to die for! Day 2 and I'm now eating a full plate of them and the vegies and OMG SOOOOOOOOOO GOOD!I'm a SUPER PICKY eater, always have been, and since going meat free and now needing gluten-free I'm even more picky. Anyone who doesn't think these are amazing ... my suggestion is try them again and fry/sauté the heck out of them, make them crispy on all sides before eating them (and possibly let them sit in the fridge fully cooked overnight then reheat).My one and only complaint, which so far as I've seen since February and needing to go gluten-free, is that these are too pricey, as are all of the gluten-free products, so between regular food's outrageous inflation and now these prices even higher, and living alone (one income)... it's hard! However, that being said, there's 100% no doubt in my mind that I will NEVER find a better plant-based, gluten-free meat type product. Beyond meat deserves a prize of excellence. These sausages are UGH-MAZE-ING!!!! No kidding, it's the first "like I grew up on" meal I've had in 7+ years. DELICIOUS! Zero difference in taste or texture (I bought the Italian style). I cannot tell these aren't spicey meat Italian sausages at all. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!!

top_review_amazon: I got sucked into the hype of the Boon Pivot but was soooo annoyed by how bulky it is, how difficult it is to fold/unfold (we have a tiny city apartment I can't leave it out all the time) ... And at that price point, woof. I decided to return it and try this Cosco stepper instead and I was immediately in love!Pro's for us:- Folds up slim (one handed) so we can tuck it behind our trash can when not in use (currently, 90%+ of the time)- Easy (albeit, 2 handed) setup! Folds out in a snap. (For comparison, boon was easy to fold out but flipping the safety bar up/down was a pain.)- No assembly was required! (Boon requires a little assembly to attach the bottom step)- It magically fits under the lip of our kitchen counter top to get even closer to the sink, yet also fits just over the lip of our bathroom counter top to get to that sink so either counter height works for us. (Boon worked with the counters we have just not this *magically.*)- I like that the safety bar can be flipped out of the way, and there's little "cup" handles on the front too for more support getting in/out of it (for the toddler). (Boon Pivot cannot move the safety bar while the child is in the tower.)- It holds up to 225lbs so we can use it as a step stool for us too, which is amazing as in our small apartment we make use of shelving, etc. for storage and always have a step stool nearby. So it's a 2-for-1 or long-term product not just something we'll use for a few years while we have a toddler. (Boon Pivot only holds up to 50lbs I think though it's a much bulkier product that seemed sturdy so I am not sure why?)Cons for us (noticeable since I previously had a Pivot to compare to):- the bottom step isn't super deep and is positioned mostly underneath the main step, so it's a little difficult for our little walker at 15 months to climb up and down/out of this thing. She'll get the hang of it eventually. (For comparison, Boon Pivot bottom step has to be installed and it is a nice deep step)- The strap used to hold the safety bar in place when not in use is strapped to the inside and I just find that cumbersome? If I was going to use the bar often I'd probably just not strap it in for easier access. (The Boon Pivot bar can flip down when not in use, but 1. It requires 2 hands to push in stupid inside buttons to unlock it and 2. You can't flip the bar up if the kid is standing on the pivot. You have to do that first and then they climb up into it. So while the strap of the Cosco bar is a tad inconvenient, it's still significantly easier to use and just makes more sense to me compared to the Pivot)- it's tall and height is not adjustable! Hopefully if you plan to fold it you have a gap next to your fridge or somewhere to put it when not in use. (Boon pivot has two height settings I believe, though it's like double the size when folded compared to cosco.)Overall, this Cosco step stool/toddler tower is half the price of the Boon Pivot with seemingly double the amount of positive attributes. Highly recommend if you're tight on space and short on height for you and your kiddo!

description_amazon: There's nothing like cooking from scratch, especially when you start with Tyson Individually Frozen Boneless Skinless Chicken Thighs. Our all-natural* chicken is juicy and tender with 16 grams of protein and 0 grams of trans fat per serving. Perfect for grilling and frying, simply cook and serve our boneless chicken thighs with BBQ sauce for a quick and delicious weeknight dinner. Includes one 2.5 lb. package of individually frozen chicken. Everything seems to turn out a whole lot better when you just keep it simple. No nonsense. Just stick to the good stuff. The 100% real stuff that makes life, and chicken, great. . Keep it real. Keep it Tyson. *Minimally processed, no artificial ingredients
top_review_amazon: Chicken Thighs are one of my favorite cuts of meat. I've order this bag of frozen thighs many times over. I have never had an issue with excess fat, freezer burn or anything. I love cooking these up to serve in a variety of dishes too.Some words of wisdom for those in need, you don't have to thaw these, but if you're going to cook them, you'll need to cook them with enough lubrication in the pan, and at a high enough heat that you cook off the excess moisture quickly. To get a beautiful golden crust on these, you have to make sure that excess moisture is gone or you're just going to end up boiling them. However, since you're cooking from frozen, you'll have to lower the temperature once you've cooked out that excess moisture, to let it cook all the way through.If you're going to thaw them first, make sure to pat them dry and maybe even salt them about 30 minutes before you cook them, covered, on the counter. Pat away the extra moisture from salting too. This will allow them to heat up slowly to room temperature so it doesn't cool the pan as much when you put them in.These are also great to throw into sauces. I've never thrown them into a sauce and had them come out chewy or tough.  You can let them unthaw in the sauce. I've also popped them onto a wire rack in the stove and if you're concerned about excess fats, it's definitely the way to go.My favorite recipe for this is pan frying the chicken from frozen, in olive oil, seasoned with garlic, salt, black pepper and onion, and then served chopped on a bed of ice berg lettuce, broccoli slaw, bacon pieces, cheese, croutons or sunflower seeds, and then drizzled with the juices of the pan--no dressing needed. Packed with flavor, and so simple.One thing I love about these bags, is that the chicken seems to be flash frozen separately, because they don't tend to stick together in one lump. It makes it really easy just to fish one or two out for a quick meal. I have no complaints, and the reviews I read where they have problems, I have to wonder if they're just struggling with proper technique when it comes to preparing these.
